faq.question: Do I need to own land before contacting ALEM?
faq.answer: No. You can contact ALEM while you are still looking. The team can discuss potential lots or teardown properties, but a specific property still needs project-level review.

faq.question: Can ALEM work with plans I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. If you already have architectural drawings, engineering, or conceptual plans, ALEM can review them, assess site feasibility, and provide an accurate construction quote.

faq.question: What happens if there is an existing home on the property?
faq.answer: ALEM handles full teardown, site preparation, utility disconnections, and grading as part of the overall build agreement.

faq.question: How is the construction cost determined?
faq.answer: Pricing is based on your specific property conditions, selected architectural plans, finish levels, and approved engineering specifications—locked in before groundbreaking.

faq.question: Who handles permits and city inspections?
faq.answer: ALEM manages all municipal filings, architectural submissions, structural reviews, inspections, and final occupancy certificate closeout.

faq.question: Can I change materials or finishes?
faq.answer: Yes. Any finish or scope adjustment is formally quoted, timeline-verified, and signed off in writing prior to execution on site.

faq.question: What is included in the finished home?
faq.answer: Every agreed interior and exterior finish—flooring, cabinetry, countertops, fixtures, appliances, mechanical connections, and paint—is fully resolved for move-in.

faq.question: Does ALEM provide a builder warranty?
faq.answer: Yes. Every ALEM custom home includes a comprehensive builder warranty package covering structural components, mechanical systems, and workmanship.

builderAccountability.title: Clear Commitments in Writing: From Scope to Warranty
builderAccountability.description: The agreement records what is included, how changes are approved, and which warranty terms apply.

commitments.description: The signed contract lists the full scope of work, transparent payment milestones, project timelines, and clear build responsibilities.
If an adjustment affects cost, scope, or schedule, it is formally reviewed and signed off before any work begins.
Coverage details, timeframes, exclusions, and warranty claim procedures are fully defined in the signed agreement.
Every required city inspection is scheduled, managed, and passed through to final permit completion and legal occupancy.
